summary: This ACLU Know Your Rights page explains legal protections for LGBTQ people in the United States across employment, housing, public accommodations, schools, restrooms, and passport and ID gender markers. It describes which federal laws (Title VII, the Fair Housing Act, Title IX) cover sexual orientation and gender identity, notes that state and local laws often provide additional protection, and gives steps to document violations and contact the ACLU for help. The page is part of a broader Know Your Rights series.
one_line: ACLU guide to LGBTQ legal protections in US employment, housing, public accommodations, schools, restrooms, and passport gender markers.
key_facts: Employers with 15 or more employees are prohibited by Title VII of the 1964 Civil Rights Act from discriminating on the basis of sex.
The Supreme Court held in 2020 in Bostock v. Clayton County that discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity is sex discrimination.
The Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity.
Housing discrimination against people with HIV/AIDS, or people perceived to have HIV/AIDS, is illegal under the Fair Housing Act's protections against disability discrimination.
HUD's Equal Access Rule bans discrimination in HUD programs on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity.
There is no federal law that bans discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity in public accommodations, like restaurants, theaters and other businesses.
Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 bans discrimination on the basis of sex by public schools.
Federal courts have held that Title IX requires public schools to respond to harassment based on appearance or behavior that doesn't conform to gender stereotypes.
Your constitutional right to privacy makes it illegal for your school to "out" you to anyone without your permission.
As of June 30, 2021, people no longer need to show medical documentation to establish or update the gender designation on a US passport.
To update a US passport gender marker, applicants fill out Form DS-11 and check the M or F box most appropriate for them.
The State Department planned to add an X designation on US passports, with information expected by the end of 2021 or early 2022.

States like Colorado, Iowa, Oregon, and Washington, and cities like San Francisco and New York City, specifically grant transgender people the right to use gender identity-appropriate restrooms in public spaces.
Cities including Austin, Texas, New York City, Philadelphia, and West Hollywood require that single-stall public restrooms be labeled as all-gender.
There is no legal obligation to have consistent gender markers on various documents, and people should obtain the marker on each document that is most comfortable for them.

entities.name: American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU)
entities.role: Provides help to people facing LGBTQ discrimination through local affiliates and the national ACLU LGBTQ & HIV Project

entities.name: ACLU LGBTQ & HIV Project
entities.role: National ACLU project that people are encouraged to contact for help weighing their options

entities.name: U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC)
entities.role: Agency where employees can file a complaint and which has taken the position that LGBTQ people are protected under Title VII

entities.name: Title VII of the 1964 Civil Rights Act
entities.role: Federal law prohibiting employment discrimination on the basis of sex, applied by some courts and the EEOC to sexual orientation and gender identity

entities.name: Bostock v. Clayton County
entities.role: 2020 Supreme Court case holding that discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity is sex discrimination

entities.name: Fair Housing Act
entities.role: Federal law prohibiting sex discrimination by most landlords, applied to sexual orientation and gender identity

entities.name: Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
entities.role: Agency whose funded housing providers are subject to its Equal Access Rule

entities.name: Federal Housing Administration (FHA)
entities.role: Agency whose insured loans and lenders are subject to HUD's Equal Access Rule

entities.name: Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972
entities.role: Federal law banning sex discrimination by public schools, applied to sexual orientation and gender identity

entities.name: State Department
entities.role: Federal agency that issues US passports and plans to add an X gender designation

entities.name: Form DS-11
entities.role: Passport application form used to establish or update the gender designation on a US passport

entities.name: Colorado, Iowa, Oregon, and Washington
entities.role: States that specifically grant transgender people the right to use gender identity-appropriate restrooms in public spaces

entities.name: San Francisco and New York City
entities.role: Cities that specifically grant transgender people the right to use gender identity-appropriate restrooms in public spaces

entities.name: Chicago
entities.role: City that lets businesses decide whether transgender patrons may use men's or women's restrooms based on the gender on their ID

entities.name: Austin, Texas, New York City, Philadelphia, and West Hollywood
entities.role: Cities that require single-stall public restrooms be labeled as all-gender
